title: 2.1.5 Sorghum Production and Management
description: Sorghum: origin, drought adaptation, production practices, management and yield

questions.question: What is the scientific name of sorghum?
questions.correctAnswer: Sorghum bicolor L.

questions.question: Where did sorghum originate?
questions.correctAnswer: Africa

questions.question: In which part of Africa is sorghum a staple food crop?
options: The coastal regions of West Africa
The forested regions of Central Africa
questions.correctAnswer: The drier parts of Africa

questions.question: How is the sorghum stalk used in rural Ethiopia?
options: As animal feed and in constructing fences and houses
As firewood for cooking and as fuel for engines
As green manure and as a cover crop
As fibre for cloth and as paper material
questions.correctAnswer: As animal feed and in constructing fences and houses

questions.question: At what altitudes are most sorghum producing areas of Ethiopia found?
questions.correctAnswer: $500$ to $1500$ m above sea level

questions.question: What kind of soil can sorghum still give reasonable yields on?
options: Soils that are too poor for other crops
Deep fertile soils rich in organic matter
Well-drained loam soils of the highlands
questions.correctAnswer: Soils that are too poor for other crops

questions.question: Which soil is stated as suitable for sorghum production?
options: Sandy soil with very low fertility
questions.correctAnswer: Well-drained, fertile clay soil

questions.question: To which parts of the country is sorghum well-adapted?
options: The drier parts of the country
The areas with regular heavy frost
questions.correctAnswer: The drier parts of the country

questions.question: What happens to sorghum during a dry period?
options: It remains dormant until soil moisture becomes sufficient
It dies immediately and needs reseeding
questions.correctAnswer: It remains dormant until soil moisture becomes sufficient

questions.question: Why is sorghum usually called 'the camel crop'?
options: It can stay dormant during dry periods and resume growth when moisture returns
It has spines like a camel's hump
It grows tall like a camel
It is mainly used to feed camels
questions.correctAnswer: It can stay dormant during dry periods and resume growth when moisture returns

questions.question: With which crops is sorghum often rotated?
options: Haricot bean, soybean, sesame and cotton
Faba bean, field pea and haricot bean
questions.correctAnswer: Haricot bean, soybean, sesame and cotton

questions.question: How many times is it necessary to cultivate the soil before planting sorghum?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 or 3 times

questions.question: How is sorghum planted?
options: Either broadcast or sown in planting rows
questions.correctAnswer: Either broadcast or sown in planting rows

questions.question: What spacing is used between planting rows for sorghum?
questions.correctAnswer: $0.5$ to $1$ metre

questions.question: What spacing is used between sorghum plants within the row?
questions.correctAnswer: About $40$ cm

questions.question: At what depth are sorghum seeds sown?
questions.correctAnswer: About $2.5$ cm

questions.question: When is the most common planting time for sorghum?
questions.correctAnswer: March to May

questions.question: When is earthing up done for sorghum and what is its purpose?
options: About a month after planting, to help the plant resist lodging due to wind
At the flowering stage, to help the plant resist drought
At harvest time, to make grain easier to thresh
Before planting, to loosen the soil for root growth
questions.correctAnswer: About a month after planting, to help the plant resist lodging due to wind

questions.question: How much nitrogen is often applied per hectare for sorghum production?
How much phosphorus is often applied per hectare for sorghum production?
What determines the fertilizer rates used for sorghum production?
options: The number of rainy days in the season
The price of sorghum in the market
questions.correctAnswer: The local soil fertility levels

questions.question: What is striga in relation to sorghum production?
options: A parasitic weed that is the major weed affecting sorghum production
A fungal disease that attacks sorghum leaves
An insect pest that feeds on sorghum grain
A mineral nutrient deficiency in sorghum fields
questions.correctAnswer: A parasitic weed that is the major weed affecting sorghum production

questions.question: What kind of damage does striga cause to sorghum?
options: Massive yield losses in sorghum producing areas
Damage to the stalk only after harvest
Reduced grain colour without affecting yield
questions.correctAnswer: Massive yield losses in sorghum producing areas

questions.question: When should hand weeding be carried out to reduce striga damage?
options: Before the sorghum starts producing seeds
After the sorghum has produced seeds
Only after the crop is harvested
At the time of seed storage
questions.correctAnswer: Before the sorghum starts producing seeds

questions.question: What should manual weeding of sorghum be combined with?
options: Crop rotation and the use of sorghum varieties resistant to pests
questions.correctAnswer: Crop rotation and the use of sorghum varieties resistant to pests

questions.question: Besides striga, what else affects sorghum production?
options: Insect pests, birds and fungal diseases such as smut
Rust and smut, and bacterial wilt
Aphids, army worm and gray leaf spot
questions.correctAnswer: Insect pests, birds and fungal diseases such as smut

questions.question: Which set of measures should pest and disease control in sorghum production involve?
options: Integrated use of crop rotation, resistant varieties and chemical methods
Only the use of resistant varieties
questions.correctAnswer: Integrated use of crop rotation, resistant varieties and chemical methods

questions.question: How long does sorghum take to mature, and when is it harvested?
options: About $4$ months, harvested when the grains start to dry with grain moisture of about $30$%
About $3$ months, harvested when the plant turns golden yellow with no green parts
About $5$ months, harvested when the grains develop a black layer
About $6$ months, harvested when the pods dry and change from green to black
questions.correctAnswer: About $4$ months, harvested when the grains start to dry with grain moisture of about $30$%

questions.question: What is the average national yield of sorghum in Ethiopia?
questions.correctAnswer: $23$ quintals ($2.3$ t) per hectare
